name: conversation
purpose: The scrolling message log of a generative AI chat. It holds the thread (`ChatMessage` items, then whatever follows the last response: suggestions, an approval card), keeps the newest message in view while the reader is at the end, and stops following the moment they scroll up to read or copy an older message — a "Scroll to the latest message" button brings them back. It is a `role="log"` whose own live behavior is off, so streamed tokens are never read one by one; instead each `ChatMessage` that finishes (or fails) hands its text to the conversation's polite live region, once. With `moreMessages`, a Load earlier messages button opens the thread and the log also emits `load-more` as the reader scrolls near the top; prepended messages never move what the reader sees. It also sets where messages sit for the whole thread (`layout`): `split` for a full chat page, `start` for a dense side panel or drawer (Cloudscape's rule for embedded surfaces). The thread is a centred reading column 752 px wide (`--container-2xl`, closest to ChatGPT's 48 rem) inside a 16 px gutter, with one even gap between messages: 36 px from `sm`, 28 px on a phone. The `composer` slot floats the composer over the bottom of the column: the thread scrolls under it behind a fade and is padded by its height; the Scroll to latest button floats just above it.
useWhen: Any surface where a person and the generative AI assistant exchange messages: the assistant page, the assistant drawer, an in-flow helper.
A transcript that grows while the reader watches it (streaming responses, tool calls appearing).
avoidWhen: A one-shot generated block on a page (a summary card, an explanation beside a chart) → render `StreamingResponse` in place.
A log of system events with timestamps and filtering → use `log-viewer`.
A list of past conversations → a `table` or `item` list; this is one thread.
A lost or resuming connection (`Reconnecting…`) → the app's state, not the log's: an `Alert` or `StatusIndicator` above the prompt input.
related: `chat-message` — the item the log holds; announces itself through this component.
`prompt-input` — the composer, floated over the bottom of the log through the `composer` slot (outside the log; only the log scrolls).
`suggestion-group` — follow-up questions after the last response, or support prompts in the empty state.

`empty-state` — what the panel shows before the first message; render it in the default slot (the thread column is at least the log's height, so `my-auto` centres it) so the composer in `composer` never remounts when the first message is sent.
bestPractices: Put the prompt input in the `composer` slot; only the log scrolls, and the thread scrolls under the composer.
Never auto-scroll while the reader is reading an older message: the component already stops following when they scroll up.
Use `layout="start"` in drawers and side panels, `split` on a full page.
Keep one conversation per surface; a second thread is a second page or a history list.
Prepend older messages in the same update that sets `loadingMore` back to `false`.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the message log. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Conversation`).

props.name: layout
props.doc: `split` puts the user's messages at the inline end (a full chat page); `start` keeps every message at the inline start (a side panel or drawer).

props.name: moreMessages
props.doc: Older messages exist above the first one. A Load earlier messages button opens the thread and the log emits `load-more` as the reader scrolls near the top.

props.name: loadingMore
props.doc: The older messages are loading; the button at the top of the thread shows its spinner and holds further `load-more` requests.

events.name: load-more
events.notes: The button's click, or the top row came within 200 px of the viewport (`new Event('load-more')`). Not repeated while `loadingMore`, nor until older messages were prepended (the first message changed); after a failed load only the button asks again.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The thread: `ChatMessage` items in order, oldest first, plus anything that follows the last response (suggestions, an approval card), or the empty state before the first message.

slots.name: composer
slots.notes: The composer floating over the bottom of the thread, in the reading column: `PromptInput`, with any status, alert or queue above it. Rendered outside the log, after it in the reading order.
